flows.name: An agent built on Cloudflare pauses for a person before a side-effecting action
flows.summary: Cloudflare's Agents documentation describes approval at three layers of an agent, for payments, deletions, external communications, bulk data operations and access-control changes; this is its expense example, with the other two layers named.

steps.what: Takes a task and decides which tools to call and in what order, adapting to intermediate results.
steps.agent: Decides its own tool use and process flow; Cloudflare distinguishes this from a workflow (a fixed path) and a co-pilot (a person acts).

steps.what: Validates the request (in the example, an expense) as a durable step.
Reports that it is waiting for approval and pauses at a durable gate (waitForApproval), which can wait for days, months or longer without keeping anything running.
Approves or rejects; the workflow records who approved.
Only after approval, carries out the action and reports it complete.

May instead put the pause at the other two layers the page names: an MCP server asking the agent's client for input (elicitation), or a connector call in model-generated code that needs approve() or reject() (Code Mode approval).
